LESSON: INTRODUCTION TO MATERIALS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Materials for Production
Topic 3.1: Introduction to Materials
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Introduction to Materials, part of Materials for Production in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How are materials used sustainably?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Introduction to Materials together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-Efficacy: learner develops effective communication skills when discussing and presenting the differences between

metallic and non-metallic materials.

28

• Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: learner develops explanation, evaluation and decision-making skills while sorting

out materials in the locality as either metallic or non-metallic.

Values:
• Responsibility: learner shows accountability as they use print or digital media to search for information on materials used in

production.

• Peace: learner displays tolerance and respect for diversity when discussing and presenting the importance of materials used

in production.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Environmental Education: learner acquires skills of protecting natural resources when brainstorming and presenting

sustainable ways of using materials in production.

Link to Other Subjects:

Social Studies: learner enhances knowledge on economic activities such as mining, fishing and trade as they search for

information on materials used in production.

Suggested learning resources

• Pre-Technical Studies handbook

• Digital devices such as; computers, laptops, smart phones, tablets among others

• Metallic and non-metallic materials

• Relevant approved textbooks and reference materials

• Photographs and pictures

• Charts
